clue.text: From Spooner, hear Kirk's mate flattened chicken

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so his name tells us to trade initial sounds

parts.note: to catch something is to hear it; it takes the SP sound from its partner
Mr Spock is Captain Kirk's crewmate in Star Trek; he takes the C sound in exchange

explanation.surface: A bizarre menu item: Captain Kirk's companion, squashed flat like a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of CATCH SPOCK and you get SPATCH COCK, written as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatchcock is a bird split down the backbone and opened out flat for grilling or roasting.

clue.text: Graduates from south and east not different

indicators.note: in a down clue, starting from the south means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: MAs, Masters of Arts, are graduates
E is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: Graduates from the south and east of the country turn out to be just alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South and east' look like two compass letters, but 'from south' tells you to read the graduates upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are identical or alike are by plain synonym not different in any respect.

clue.text: One pointing to yellow climbing plant

parts.note: an arrow is a sign that points the way

indicators.note: in a down clue, something climbing goes upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: Someone points out a yellow climbing plant, perhaps a creeper on a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing plant' looks like one phrase, but 'climbing' turns TO and OR upside down in this down clue. OR is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a tropical plant whose starchy rhizome is ground into a thickening flour.

clue.text: Abandonments from vessel on ocean still at sea

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel

indicators.note: to be at sea is to be confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Things left adrift by a ship becalmed on the ocean, still out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship to match the sea, but here it is a humble can; 'on' places it above the rest in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: When planned events are called off they are abandoned, so abandonments are cancellations.

clue.text: Woman from capital leaving centre on railway track

indicators.note: something leaving its centre loses the middle, so the central letter drops out

parts.note: Cairo is the capital of Egypt; its middle letter I goes
a railway line is a track

explanation.surface: A woman from a capital city sets off from the centre along a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital is Egypt's; 'on' places the shortened city above the track, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Caroline is a common female first name, and a woman is the usual crossword cue for one.

clue.text: Corgis occasionally avoided Queen Elizabeth's herald

indicators.note: if letters are avoided only now and then, every other one is skipped and the rest kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: The late Queen's corgis now and then gave her herald a wide berth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's famous corgis are just letter fodder; ER is the standard abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was the official who announced public news in the street, acting as a herald.

clue.text: Exchange Shrek's home with medium shed

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: the ogre Shrek lives in a swamp in the films
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: An estate-agent pitch: trade the ogre's home for a medium-sized garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun for the swap, but it is a verb removing the M.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing for another is to trade them, which is the everyday meaning of the verb here.

clue.text: Part of fingerprint which person's found on both hands

parts.note: 'which person' is who
R and L, right and left

explanation.surface: A forensic question: whose prints appear on both of the suspect's hands?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which person's' gives WHO, the 's standing for 'is'; R and L are right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A whorl is a spiral ridge pattern, one of the three basic shapes found in human fingerprints.

clue.text: Clean up some time with relative restraining one dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to mop is to clean
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: a nan is a grandmother
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Tidying up after spending time with Granny, who has her one dog on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean up' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'up' reverses MOP; NAN then holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pomeranian is a small fluffy toy breed of dog originating from the Pomerania region.

clue.text: Lip reflected in cooking liquid

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

parts.note: a lip is the rim of a vessel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A face, or a pan's edge, reflected in the liquid simmering on the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the lip, but it is part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirin is a sweet Japanese rice wine used as a seasoning liquid in cooking.

clue.text: Gent upset with this meteorological event might be remonstrating

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the full set of letters that the combined anagram must make
these letters are taken out of the full set

explanation.surface: A gentleman, put out by the weather, is complaining loudly about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: GENT plus the answer, jumbled, makes REMONSTRATING, so remove G, E, N, T from that word and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a weather occurrence of heavy rain and wind, the kind a forecaster tracks.

clue.text: Reportedly noted Pittsburgh team players grabbing attention

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so we go by how the words are said

parts.note: something noted has been seen
the Pittsburgh Steelers are an American football team

explanation.surface: The Pittsburgh team's players have made a name for themselves, it's said.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEN and STEELERS, said together, sound like the phrase for actors who outshine the rest of the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Scene-stealers are performers who draw the audience's attention away from others on stage or screen.

clue.text: Cyclist, one distributing cards, is shrewd trader

parts.note: a wheeler is one who wheels, a cyclist
the dealer hands out the cards

explanation.surface: A cyclist who deals cards on the side turns out to be a sharp operator.
explanation.walkthrough: The two halves of the hyphenated answer come straight from the two descriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeler-dealer is a person who does business through clever, often slightly dubious, bargaining and scheming.

clue.text: Dashing scout striking out on hike

indicators.note: striking something off a list removes it, so letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
the letters struck off
someone out on a hike is rambling

explanation.surface: A scout rushes off as he sets out on a hike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking out' reads as setting off, but it strikes OUT from SCOUT, leaving SC; rambling is British for country walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambling means moving hurriedly and urgently, which is what dashing about involves.

clue.text: One hundred staff around plot farming area

parts.note: Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
a plot is a plan

explanation.surface: A hundred farmhands work round a plot of land on the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a piece of land, fitting the farm, but here it is a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Cropland is land used for growing crops, an area given over to arable farming.

clue.text: Stun college fellow, describing depleted finance

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: a dean is a senior fellow of a college

indicators.note: something depleted has been emptied out, leaving only its shell

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A college fellow is stunned on hearing about the college's dwindling funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' here means drawing a line around, as in describing a circle, so DEAN goes round the hollowed finance.
explanation.definitionFit: A very loud noise can stun the ears, temporarily making a person unable to hear.

clue.text: Anticipated revolutionary of note imprisoning king

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to imprison is to lock up inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: note means fame, as in a person of note
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A famous revolutionary, seen coming, locks up the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary of note' reads as a famous rebel, but 'revolutionary' only turns OF round, and 'note' alone is fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anticipated was expected beforehand, that is, known about in advance of it happening.

clue.text: Aberrant merganser abandoning northern lake

indicators.note: aberrant means straying from the normal course, so the letters wander out of order
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a merganser is a fish-eating duck
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A wayward duck leaves a lake in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Grasmere is a lake in England's Lake District, in the north-west, which makes 'northern lake' look like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasmere is one of the small lakes of the English Lake District, near Wordsworth's former home.

clue.text: Clever, like one being taught endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: as means like
a tutee is someone receiving tuition

explanation.surface: A bright pupil, the kind of student who never stops learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' seems to describe constant study, but it trims the last letter of TUTEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astute means having sharp judgement and shrewdness, a close synonym for clever.

clue.text: Spies must accept service with right rules

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a religious service is a rite
R is short for right

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents must go along with service, along with the right rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests duty in the agency, but it is a church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are standards used for judging, so they act as rules or principles for a decision.

clue.text: Doctor squeezing down head of spot with stickiness hit the roof

indicators.note: to squeeze something is to grip it tightly inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Bones is Dr McCoy's nickname in Star Trek
feeling down is feeling low

indicators.note: the head is the top, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter
tack is the sticky quality of glue or paint

explanation.surface: A doctor squeezing a sticky spot makes the patient furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is not DR or MO but Bones, the Enterprise's medic, continuing the Star Trek theme of 1-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms describe suddenly losing one's temper and erupting in an outburst of anger.

clue.text: Dined on sandwiches made of grain

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between two slices, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: taken as written
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone lunched on sandwiches made from wholegrain bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like the food that was eaten, but it is a verb with ON as the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaten describes something made from oats, a cereal grain, as in oaten cakes.

clue.text: Instruct European to replace second in change

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes the place of another

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a mo is a moment, a second
to modify is to change

explanation.surface: An order telling a European to substitute for someone halfway through a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like the second letter, but it is MO, short for moment, which E replaces at the front of MODIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify someone is to improve them morally or intellectually by teaching, which is instructing them.

clue.text: One tweeting interminably with it

indicators.note: without termination means without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a chick is a young bird, which tweets

explanation.surface: Someone forever posting on social media and being fashionable with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeting' suggests social media, but this is birdsong from a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means fashionable and up to date, which is what stylish chic describes.

clue.text: Part of the body involved in skin test inevitably

indicators.note: something involved in a thing is wrapped up within it, so the answer is inside the following words

parts.note: running across the three words

explanation.surface: A medical note: which organ is affected when a skin test is done, as it inevitably is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'skin' through 'test' into the start of 'inevitably'.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestine is the long tube of the gut, a major organ inside the human body.

clue.text: Confidence returned winning heart of lucky date

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters run backwards
to win something is to gain and hold it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: hope is a confident expectation

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter counts

parts.note: the central letter

explanation.surface: Confidence came back after winning the heart of a lucky date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' suggests a romantic partner, but it is a point in time.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a particular period or moment in history, so it can stand for a date in time.

clue.text: Possible guess in Battleships is missing

parts.note: a shot is called as a column letter first
then a row number, here 1

explanation.surface: In a game of Battleships, a guess that misses the target ships.
explanation.walkthrough: In Battleships each shot is called as a column letter plus a row number, so G1 reads as G ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is gone has disappeared and cannot be found, so it is missing.

clue.text: Speedy promoters working pitch regularly

parts.note: hypers are people who hype things up
a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Fast-talking promoters at work making a regular sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' looks like a sales pitch, but only its even letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersonic describes speeds of more than five times the speed of sound, extremely fast.
